query: An equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy has a simple solid-solution structure and favorable plasticity and machinability but relatively low hardness and strength, while its microstructure and deformation behavior remain insufficiently understood. Under hardness testing and mechanical loading of this starting state, what single intervention could overcome the strength and hardness limitation while retaining its favorable mechanical characteristics? State the proposed intervention, its mechanism, the predicted measurable change relative to the unmodified alloy, its applicable processing and test conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a microstructural and mechanical experiment that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Aging treatment of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy at 600–800°C for 4–12 hours will induce coherent Ti-rich precipitates (B2 or Laves phase) within the FCC matrix, significantly increasing hardness and yield strength while retaining ductility through precipitation hardening and dislocation pinning mechanisms.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy with simple FCC solid-solution structure, favorable plasticity and machinability, but relatively low hardness and strength.
generation.intervention: Solution annealing followed by aging heat treatment at 600–800°C for 4–12 hours to promote coherent Ti-rich precipitate formation.
generation.conditions: Aging temperature: 600–800°C; Aging time: 4–12 hours; Cooling: Air cooling or furnace cooling; Pre-treatment: Solution annealing at 1000–1100°C for 1 hour followed by water quenching.
generation.structural_mediator: Coherent Ti-rich precipitates (B2 or Laves phase) with nanoscale size (10–100 nm) distributed within the FCC matrix.
generation.mechanism: Precipitation hardening via Orowan looping and dislocation pinning by coherent precipitates, combined with solid solution strengthening from Ti segregation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Hardness increase of 30–50% (from ~200 HV to ~280–300 HV), yield strength increase of 40–60% (from ~300 MPa to ~420–480 MPa), while maintaining ductility >15% elongation.
generation.baseline: As-cast or solution-annealed equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy with FCC structure, hardness ~200 HV, yield strength ~300 MPa, elongation >20%.
generation.boundary: Aging temperature must not exceed 850°C to avoid precipitate coarsening and loss of coherency; aging time must not exceed 24 hours to prevent over-aging and embrittlement.
generation.uncertainty: The exact precipitate phase (B2 vs Laves) and optimal aging parameters may vary depending on initial microstructure and cooling rate; potential for reduced ductility if precipitates become incoherent or too large.
generation.falsification_experiment: Perform aging treatment at 700°C for 8 hours on CoCrFeNiTi alloy, then measure hardness, yield strength, and elongation. If hardness increases by <10% or elongation drops below 10%, the hypothesis is falsified. Additionally, use TEM to confirm absence of coherent precipitates after aging.
